# davidfacer.com

A personal professional portfolio and research hub. One person: David
Facer. Two subject areas: enterprise architecture and AI-native
operating practice, and open-source intelligence research.

This file is a guide for automated readers. It says what exists here and
where. It does not reproduce the site — every page below serves its own
readable text, except where marked CARRIED, which means the page itself
delivers nothing to a reader without a browser and the substance is
given here instead.

WRITTEN BY HAND on 2026-09-12. It is not generated from anything, so it
can go stale. If a line here disagrees with the page it describes, the
page is right.

---

  Professional overview — background, focus, and how the two subject
  areas relate. Serves its own text.

/professional/cv/
  Full curriculum vitae: roles, dates, scope of responsibility.
  Substantial, and the most detailed single document on this domain.
  Serves its own text.

## Research

/blackseamonitor/
  Black Sea Monitor. Open-source intelligence research on Black Sea
  maritime activity, including the methodology behind it. The longest
  document on this site and entirely server-rendered; a reader that can
  fetch one page here should fetch this one.

/wire/
  Present but not currently publishing. Listed so an automated reader
  that finds it knows that state is intended rather than broken.

## Assessment tool

/complexity-sovereignty-assessment/
  CARRIED — this page is a client-rendered application. It returns an
  empty document shell to anything that does not execute JavaScript, so
  a pointer alone would send you to a blank page. What it is:

  The Complexity–Sovereignty Assessment is an interactive
  self-assessment. It asks an organization to place itself on two
  axes — the complexity it is carrying, and the degree of sovereignty
  it holds over its own systems and decisions — and returns a reading
  of where those two sit relative to each other. It is a diagnostic
  instrument for a leadership team to use on itself, not a scored
  benchmark against other organizations, and it is free to use.

  A reader that can execute JavaScript should load the page itself;
  this summary is not a substitute for the instrument.

## Related sites, separately published

https://aimaturitymodels.com
  The AI-Native Maturity Model family. Four published maturity models —
  SDLC, PDLC, Product Prioritization, and Enterprise Architecture —
  each with a whole-model view, plus a layered governance model and a
  set of function models. This is a separate site with its own
  content.

  It publishes its own machine-readable digest, which CARRIES the model
  content in full rather than pointing at it:

    https://aimaturitymodels.com/llms.txt

  An automated reader wanting the models themselves should fetch that
  file, not this one.

https://maturitymodel.substack.com/
  Substack publication. External platform, separately published.

https://superdtf.substack.com/
  Substack publication. External platform, separately published.

## Notes for automated readers

- Everything listed here is public. Nothing on this domain requires
  sign-in to read.
- /sitemap.xml lists this domain's main pages. It does not list the
  prototype destinations above, which are on a subdomain, nor /wire.
  This file is the more complete inventory of the two.
- No identifier is named here that a reader cannot follow. Where this
  practice has internal documents, they are not referenced.
